nodes.name: Event catalogue
nodes.summary: Every event an app can subscribe to, split into asynchronous notifications and synchronous request-and-answer calls, with the permission each one requires.
nodes.detail: The catalogue is two plain classes of string constants. WebhookEventAsyncType lists the fire-and-forget events (order, checkout, product, customer, app lifecycle and so on) and WebhookEventSyncType lists the events where Saleor waits for the app's answer (payments, transactions, taxes, shipping methods, stored payment methods). Each class builds an EVENT_MAP of name, required permission and, for some asynchronous events, an is_deferred_payload flag; CHOICES, PERMISSIONS and ALL are derived from it. Webhook selection, manifest validation, the GraphQL enums and the circuit breaker all read these maps.

nodes.name: Payload generation
nodes.summary: Builds what a webhook carries: either the app's own GraphQL subscription query run against the event object, or a fixed legacy JSON payload.
nodes.detail: Modern webhooks store a GraphQL subscription query. When an event fires, Saleor builds a fake request scoped to the receiving app, executes the query against the schema with the root value (event_type, object), and the resolved data becomes the payload, so an app only receives fields it asked for and is allowed to read. The Subscription type and WEBHOOK_TYPES_MAP map every event to its GraphQL type. Older webhooks without a query get hand-built payloads from webhook/payloads.py, serialized with a Django serializer. Dataloaders are shared across apps during one trigger so the same data is not loaded twice.

nodes.name: Asynchronous delivery
nodes.summary: Turns an event into stored payloads and delivery rows, then hands each delivery to a Celery task that sends it with exponential back-off retries.
nodes.detail: trigger_webhooks_async splits the matching webhooks into legacy and subscription webhooks. Legacy payloads and immediate subscription payloads are written as EventPayload plus EventDelivery rows in one database transaction. For events flagged as deferred, only EventDelivery rows are written and a generate_deferred_payloads task builds the payloads later from a database replica. Every ready delivery is queued as send_webhook_request_async on a Celery queue chosen by the target scheme, with an Amazon Simple Queue Service (SQS) message group per app. The task signs and sends the payload, records an attempt, retries failures other than 3xx and 4xx answers up to 5 times with a 10 second base back-off, and deletes the delivery and payload once it succeeds.

nodes.name: Synchronous webhooks
nodes.summary: Calls an app and waits for its JSON answer, for payments, transactions, taxes and shipping, with response caching, schema validation and a circuit breaker.
nodes.detail: trigger_webhook_sync_promise builds a delivery (from the subscription query or a static payload), then send_webhook_request_sync posts it over HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol) and parses the body as JSON; a failed or unparsable answer returns None. Deliveries for synchronous events are usually not saved unless they fail. A cached variant stores answers for 5 minutes and remembers a failure for 1 second. Transaction action requests (charge, refund, cancel) run as a Celery task so they can retry on 5xx answers. Pydantic response schemas validate what payment, transaction, tax and shipping apps send back. When BREAKER_BOARD_ENABLED is set, the promise function is wrapped by the circuit breaker.

nodes.name: Transport, signing and metrics
nodes.summary: Sends one payload to Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP), Amazon Simple Queue Service (SQS) or Google Cloud Pub/Sub targets, signs it, records attempts and retries, and emits OpenTelemetry metrics.
nodes.detail: send_webhook_using_scheme_method picks a sender from the target URL scheme: http and https go through the hardened Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) client with Saleor-Event, Saleor-Domain, Saleor-Signature and Saleor-Api-Url headers; awssqs URLs carry credentials and a queue path for boto3; gcpubsub URLs name a topic. The payload signature is an HMAC (hash-based message authentication code) SHA-256 when the webhook has a secret key, otherwise a detached JSON Web Signature from Saleor's key. Helpers create and update EventDeliveryAttempt rows, mark deliveries of inactive apps as failed, compute Celery retry countdowns and clean up delivered payloads and their files.

nodes.name: Circuit breaker for sync webhooks
nodes.summary: Stops calling an app's synchronous webhooks for a cooldown when too many of them fail, counting successes and errors per app in Redis.
nodes.detail: The breaker board keeps one state per app: closed, open or half-open. Each monitored synchronous call registers a total event and, when the answer is None, an error event in Redis sorted sets that expire after 5 minutes. With at least 100 errors and 35 percent failures the breaker opens; after a 2 minute cooldown it goes half-open, where 20 errors at 30 percent re-open it and 50 successes close it. While open, calls resolve to None without a request, except dry-run events which still run. Only events listed in BREAKER_BOARD_SYNC_EVENTS are monitored, and the whole board is off unless BREAKER_BOARD_ENABLED is true.

nodes.name: Observability events
nodes.summary: Buffers API-call and delivery-attempt reports in Redis and ships them in batches to apps subscribed to the OBSERVABILITY event.
nodes.detail: When OBSERVABILITY_ACTIVE is on, the GraphQL view reports each application programming interface (API) call and the webhook tasks report each delivery attempt. A report becomes a JSON event with headers filtered and sensitive values masked, request and response bodies truncated to OBSERVABILITY_MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE, and payloads of subscriptions touching sensitive fields replaced by a mask. Events are zlib-compressed into a capped Redis list. A periodic Celery task pops batches and posts them, concatenated into one JSON array for Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) targets or one message each for queue targets, to every active OBSERVABILITY webhook. Webhook lists are cached for 2 minutes.

nodes.name: Webhook subscriptions and selection
nodes.summary: The Webhook and WebhookEvent tables, the queries that pick active webhooks of active, permitted apps for an event, and custom header rules.
nodes.detail: A Webhook belongs to an App and stores the target URL, optional secret key, subscription query, up to 5 custom headers, channel slugs parsed from the query's channel filter and how deferred payloads are generated. WebhookEvent rows list its event types. Selection reads the replica: a webhook qualifies when it is active, its app is active, not removed (except for APP_DELETED) and holds the event's permission, and it subscribes to the event or to ANY_EVENTS. App lifecycle events go only to the affected app's own webhooks. Channel-filtered webhooks are dropped when the object's channel is not in their list.

nodes.name: Apps and installation
nodes.summary: Installed apps, their hashed tokens, permissions, dashboard extensions and problems, and the background installation from a manifest URL.
nodes.detail: An App holds identity, URLs from its manifest, permissions and an is_active flag; AppToken stores a Django password hash of the raw token plus its last 4 characters; AppExtension describes where the app renders inside the dashboard. Installing creates an AppInstallation job; a Celery task fetches the manifest, validates it with a Pydantic schema and extra checks, creates the App, extensions, Webhooks and WebhookEvents, posts a fresh token to the app's tokenTargetUrl and fires APP_INSTALLED. Deleting is a soft delete; a periodic task removes apps and their deliveries in batches after DELETE_APP_TTL (default 1 day).

nodes.name: GraphQL for apps, webhooks and plugins
nodes.summary: The queries and mutations staff, the dashboard and apps use to install apps, manage tokens and webhooks, retry deliveries and configure plugins.
nodes.detail: Three schema modules are merged into the application programming interface (API) by the core schema: app queries and mutations (install, fetch manifest, tokens, activate, problems, re-enable synchronous webhooks), webhook queries and mutations (create, update, delete, dry run, trigger, retry a delivery, sample payload) and plugin queries and the pluginUpdate mutation, plus the deprecated externalNotificationTrigger. Most write operations need the MANAGE_APPS or MANAGE_PLUGINS permission; an app can manage its own webhooks.

nodes.name: App GraphQL API
nodes.summary: App, AppToken, AppExtension and AppInstallation types, their resolvers and dataloaders, and the app mutations.
nodes.detail: Resolvers read installed, non-removed apps only. The App type exposes an accessToken field: for third-party apps, when a staff user asks, it returns a short-lived JSON Web Token (JWT) the app's iframe frontend can use to call Saleor on that user's behalf; apps holding MANAGE_APPS are refused. AppByTokenLoader authenticates app requests by matching the last 4 characters and checking the password hash, then caches the token-to-app mapping. The App type also reports circuit breaker state from the breaker storage.

nodes.name: Webhook GraphQL API
nodes.summary: Webhook, WebhookEvent, EventDelivery and EventDeliveryAttempt types, the generated event enums, and the webhook mutations.
nodes.detail: WebhookCreate and WebhookUpdate validate the subscription query, extract the channel filter, check custom headers and derive the event list from the query when none is given. WebhookDryRun runs a subscription query against a real object without sending anything; WebhookTrigger sends one real delivery to one webhook; EventDeliveryRetry re-queues a failed delivery through the plugin manager. Enums for asynchronous and synchronous event types are generated from the event catalogue.

nodes.name: Plugin and notification GraphQL API
nodes.summary: Plugin queries and pluginUpdate, the dataloaders that give every request its plugin manager, and the deprecated externalNotificationTrigger.
nodes.detail: get_plugin_manager_promise builds one PluginsManager per requestor (app, user or anonymous) per request through dataloaders. The plugins query aggregates global and per-channel configurations and hides secret fields; pluginUpdate saves configuration for a plugin, globally or for one channel. externalNotificationTrigger serializes customers or orders and passes them to plugins' notify method.

nodes.name: Plugin manager
nodes.summary: Loads the plugins listed in settings.PLUGINS, global or per channel, and runs each hook method across them in order, chaining their return values.
nodes.detail: PluginsManager imports every class path from settings.PLUGINS lazily: plugins with CONFIGURATION_PER_CHANNEL False load once globally, the rest load per channel slug with their PluginConfiguration row (or defaults). A hook call such as order_created or calculate_checkout_total runs the same-named method on every active plugin for that channel; each receives previous_value and returns a new one, and plugins without the method are skipped. Webhook delivery hangs off this mechanism through WebhookPlugin. The manager also routes the /plugins/ Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) endpoints to a plugin's webhook method.

nodes.name: Webhook plugin bridge
nodes.summary: WebhookPlugin, always active, turns every plugin hook into webhook deliveries: asynchronous for notifications, synchronous for payments and transactions.
nodes.detail: For each asynchronous hook it looks up matching webhooks (or uses the ones the caller already selected), filters channel-scoped subscriptions, prepares a lazy legacy payload generator and calls trigger_webhooks_async, sometimes on a dedicated Celery queue such as ORDER_WEBHOOK_EVENTS_CELERY_QUEUE_NAME. For synchronous hooks it finds the app's webhook for the event, builds a static payload as fallback and calls trigger_webhook_sync_promise, then parses the answer into payment gateways, gateway responses, stored payment methods or transaction session results. Payment gateway ids use the form app:<identifier>:<external id>.

nodes.name: Email plugins and notifications
nodes.summary: Two built-in plugins that send staff and customer emails over the store's Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) server from Handlebars templates, through Celery tasks.
nodes.detail: AdminEmailPlugin (global) and UserEmailPlugin (per channel) implement the notify hook. Each maps notify event names to a function that queues a Celery task with the payload, SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) settings and the template from configuration or a bundled default. The task renders subject and body with pybars and sends through Django's SMTP backend, adding a plain-text part. Templates can be overridden per plugin configuration and are stored as EmailTemplate rows.

WebhookEventAsyncType also defines ANY ('any_events'), which subscribes a webhook to all asynchronous events. Order, draft order and a few other events set is_deferred_payload so their subscription payloads are built in a background task. WebhookEventSyncType adds groupings such as PAYMENT_EVENTS and ALLOWED_IN_CIRCULAR_QUERY.

The generator parses the query, executes it with allow_subscriptions and root (event_type, subscribable_object), subscribes to the resulting observable and takes the first item. If the root field is 'event' the data is returned as is, otherwise wrapped as {'data': {...}}. Field errors are attached under 'errors'; a query that fails validation yields None and no delivery. nodes.summary: Sends a synchronous delivery and returns the app's parsed JSON answer, or None when the request failed or the body was not JSON.

nodes.name: _send_webhook_request_sync()

After the call it updates the attempt and delivery status, reports the attempt to observability, saves the delivery and attempt only when unsuccessful, and deletes them when successful. nodes.name: trigger_webhook_sync_promise()
nodes.summary: Builds a delivery from the subscription query (unsaved) or the static payload, then sends it; the function other areas call for sync events.

nodes.name: trigger_webhook_sync_promise_if_not_cached()
nodes.summary: Returns a cached answer when present, skips the call for 1 second after a failure, and otherwise calls the app and caches its answer.
nodes.detail: The cache key combines app id, target URL, event type and a SHA-256 of the caller's cache data. Answers are cached for the caller's timeout or 5 minutes by default; a None answer stores the WEBHOOK_FAILURE sentinel for 1 second. Used for shipping methods and stored payment methods.

nodes.name: Sync subscription delivery builder
nodes.summary: Resolves the subscription payload for a synchronous event and builds the EventPayload and EventDelivery, saving them only when asked.

nodes.name: trigger_transaction_request()
nodes.summary: Creates a saved delivery for a charge, refund or cancel request to the transaction's owning app and queues handle_transaction_request_task.
nodes.detail: Fails the request with a transaction event when the transaction has no app owner, the app has no webhook for the event, or no payload could be generated, and then recalculates the checkout's refundable amount. The task is queued with call_event so it waits for the surrounding database transaction to commit.

nodes.name: handle_transaction_request_task
nodes.summary: Celery task that sends a transaction action request, retries on 5xx answers (5 retries, 10 second back-off) and records the app's answer as a transaction event.

nodes.name: Legacy payment answer parsers
nodes.summary: Parses answers to the legacy payment webhooks: the gateway list for PAYMENT_LIST_GATEWAYS and gateway responses for authorize, capture and refund.
nodes.detail: parse_list_payment_gateways_response keeps entries that have an id and prefixes each id with the app, so later payment calls route back to that app. parse_payment_action_response maps the answer's error, amount, psp reference, payment method details and action-required data onto a GatewayResponse, taking the currency from the request and defaulting the amount to the requested one. Used only by the legacy payment flow in WebhookPlugin.

nodes.name: Stored payment method answer handling
nodes.summary: Validates answers for listing and deleting stored payment methods and tokenization sessions, and invalidates the cached list.
nodes.detail: Validates the app's answer with the payment response schemas and turns each valid stored method into PaymentMethodData with an app-prefixed id; an invalid answer is logged and treated as an empty list. It also builds the cache key data for the listing call, deletes that cache entry after a deletion request, and maps tokenization answers (success, pending, failed) to result objects.

nodes.name: Synchronous answer schemas
nodes.summary: Pydantic models that validate what apps answer to transaction, tax, shipping and stored payment method webhooks, also exported as JSON schemas.
nodes.detail: Each schema checks types, amounts and enum values and is tolerant where possible: annotations such as skip_invalid and default_if_invalid drop or default bad optional fields instead of failing the whole answer. parse_validation_error turns a Pydantic error into a readable message for transaction events and logs. SCHEMAS_TO_EXPORT lists the models a management command writes out as JSON schema files for app developers.

nodes.name: Transaction answer schemas
nodes.summary: Schemas for transaction charge, refund and cancel answers (synchronous success or failure, or asynchronous) and transaction session results.
nodes.detail: TransactionBaseSchema defines the common fields: psp reference, amount, time (defaults to now), external URL, message and actions, with lenient defaults for missing values. Success, failure and asynchronous variants per action set which result values are allowed. Session schemas add the session results such as action required, and PaymentGatewayInitializeSessionSchema accepts the gateway's data blob.

nodes.name: CalculateTaxesSchema
nodes.summary: Validates a tax app's answer: shipping price and tax rate, and per-line net and gross totals and tax rates.

nodes.name: Shipping answer schemas
nodes.summary: Schemas for shipping methods listed by an app and shipping methods an app excludes for a checkout or order.
nodes.detail: ShippingMethodSchema requires an id, a name, a non-negative amount and a currency, with optional minimum and maximum delivery days, description and metadata. ListShippingMethodsSchema is a root list of those. FilterShippingMethodsSchema reads excluded_methods, each with an id and reason, for the filter-shipping-methods events.

nodes.name: Stored payment method schemas
nodes.summary: Schemas for stored payment methods, their deletion and payment method tokenization answers.
nodes.detail: Schemas for stored payment methods carry id, supported flows, type, name, data and optional credit card details, and skip individual invalid methods with a logged message instead of rejecting the list. Tokenization schemas accept success, pending or failed results with the fields each one needs, and the delete-requested schema reads result and error.

nodes.name: Breaker board
nodes.summary: Evaluates and changes per-app circuit breaker state and wraps the synchronous webhook promise function with it.
nodes.detail: Thresholds are module constants, not settings. validate_sync_events refuses to start when BREAKER_BOARD_SYNC_EVENTS is empty, names an unknown event, or BREAKER_BOARD_DRY_RUN_SYNC_EVENTS lists an event that is not monitored. Every state change clears the app's counters, logs to the breaker_board logger and increments an OpenTelemetry counter.
facts: Half-open: re-opens at 20 errors and 30 percent, closes after 50 successes

nodes.name: BreakerBoard
nodes.summary: Holds storage and thresholds, decides closed, open and half-open transitions, and registers successes and errors per app.

nodes.name: BreakerBoard.update_breaker_state()
nodes.summary: Reads the app's state and counts and applies the transition rules: closed to open, open to half-open after cooldown, half-open to open or closed.

nodes.name: BreakerBoard.wrap_promise_func()
nodes.summary: Wraps trigger_webhook_sync_promise: skips monitored calls while open, and counts a None answer as an error and anything else as a success.

nodes.name: RedisStorage
nodes.summary: Keeps breaker state as 'state|changed_at' and events as Redis sorted sets scored by time, trimmed to the window on every write.
nodes.detail: Keys look like bbrs-<app id>-state, bbrs-<app id>-error and bbrs-<app id>-total. register_event removes entries older than the window and adds a random member in one pipeline; counts are ZCARD. Redis errors are logged as warnings and treated as a closed breaker with zero counts, so a Redis outage never blocks webhooks.

nodes.name: Observability reporters
nodes.summary: Context managers and functions that turn application programming interface (API) calls and delivery attempts into buffered observability events.
nodes.detail: report_api_call and report_view keep one ApiCall per request in an asgiref Local and report it when the outermost block exits; report_gql_operation collects each GraphQL operation into it. Only app requests are reported unless OBSERVABILITY_REPORT_ALL_API_CALLS is set. Nothing is generated when no OBSERVABILITY webhook exists. Truncation errors and buffer overflows drop the event with a warning instead of failing the request.

nodes.name: report_event_delivery_attempt()
nodes.summary: Queues an observability event for one webhook delivery attempt, including the next retry time when known.

nodes.name: report_api_call() and report_view()
nodes.summary: Wraps the GraphQL view so each Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) request and its GraphQL operations become one observability event.

nodes.name: get_webhooks()
nodes.summary: Returns active OBSERVABILITY webhooks, cached in process memory and in the Django cache for 2 minutes.

nodes.name: put_event() and pop_events_with_remaining_size()
nodes.summary: Pushes one generated event into the Redis buffer, and pops a batch together with how many further batches remain.

nodes.name: RedisBuffer
nodes.summary: A capped, expiring Redis list of zlib-compressed events: push trims to the size limit, pop reads a batch with RPOP in one pipeline.

nodes.name: Observability payloads
nodes.summary: Builds API-call and delivery-attempt event JSON in camelCase, truncating bodies to fit the byte limit and anonymizing sensitive data.
nodes.detail: Both generators build a typed dictionary, measure its JSON size and fail with a truncation error when even the fixed fields exceed the byte limit. Remaining bytes are shared out to the large text parts, which JsonTruncText cuts by encoded size. Headers pass through the obfuscation filter, keys are converted to camelCase and the result is dumped as compact JSON bytes.

nodes.name: generate_event_delivery_attempt_payload()
nodes.summary: Describes one attempt: status, duration, request and response headers, response body, delivery payload, webhook and app, within the byte limit.
facts: Gives the subscription query a quarter of the remaining bytes and the response body half of what is left

nodes.name: Observability obfuscation
nodes.summary: Keeps only allowed headers and masks sensitive ones, and masks results or payloads of queries that select sensitive GraphQL fields.
nodes.detail: filter_and_hide_headers keeps only headers on the allowed list and replaces sensitive ones with '***'. A GraphQL validation rule walks a query, including fragments, and flags any selection of a field listed as sensitive for its type. If an application programming interface (API) call's query or a subscription query touches such a field, the whole result or payload is replaced by the mask.

nodes.name: Webhook models
nodes.summary: The Webhook and WebhookEvent tables and the payload generation choice.
nodes.detail: Webhook.target_url accepts http, https, awssqs and gcpubsub URLs, validated by AppURLValidator. A Generalized Inverted Index (GIN) index on filterable_channel_slugs supports channel filtering; identifier is unique per app and must not be blank. payload_generation is read once when deliveries are created, so changing it never affects queued work.

nodes.name: Webhook
nodes.summary: One subscription of an app: name, target URL, active flag, secret key, subscription query, custom headers, channel slugs, identifier, payload generation.

nodes.name: WebhookEvent
nodes.summary: One event type a webhook subscribes to, indexed by event type for selection queries.

nodes.name: Webhook selection queries
nodes.summary: Finds the webhooks that should receive an event, enforcing app activity, removal and permission rules on the read replica.
nodes.detail: All reads go to the replica connection because selection never depends on writes made in the same request. Single-event selection uses Exists subqueries for the app and for the WebhookEvent row. Multi-event selection loads WebhookEvent pairs once, then filters apps and permissions in Python, which is how order code fetches webhooks for several events in one go.

nodes.name: get_webhooks_for_event()
nodes.summary: Returns active webhooks for one event, optionally limited to app ids or identifiers, with app permissions prefetched.

nodes.summary: Builds the filter: webhook active, app active and not removed, app holds the event's permission, and webhook subscribes to the event or ANY.

nodes.name: get_webhooks_for_multiple_events()
nodes.summary: Computes webhooks for several events in a few queries, returning an entry for every event even when it has no webhooks.

nodes.name: get_webhooks_for_app_lifecycle_event()
nodes.summary: Returns only the affected app's own webhooks for APP_INSTALLED, APP_UPDATED, APP_DELETED and APP_STATUS_CHANGED, even if it is inactive.

nodes.name: filter_webhooks_for_channel()
nodes.summary: Drops subscription webhooks whose channel filter does not include the object's channel; webhooks without a filter pass.

nodes.name: custom_headers_validator()
nodes.summary: Allows at most 5 custom headers named X-*, Authorization* or BrokerProperties, checks characters and length, and lowercases the keys.

nodes.name: App models
nodes.summary: The App, AppToken, AppExtension, AppProblem and AppInstallation tables and the app permission checks.
nodes.detail: App.get_permissions caches 'app_label.codename' strings and returns none for an inactive app, so deactivating an app removes all its rights at once. AppQueryset.for_event_type filters apps by subscribed event and permission. AppInstallation extends the Job model (status and message) and keeps the requested permissions until the task finishes.

nodes.name: App
nodes.summary: An installed app: identifier, name, type (local or thirdparty), URLs from its manifest, permissions, is_active, is_installed, removed_at, metadata.

nodes.name: AppToken
nodes.summary: An app's application programming interface (API) token, stored as a Django password hash with its last 4 characters for lookup; the raw token is shown only once.
facts: Raw tokens come from oauthlib generate_token, 30 characters

nodes.name: AppExtension
nodes.summary: A place where the app renders inside the dashboard: label, URL, mount point, target (popup by default), settings and permissions.

nodes.name: AppProblem
nodes.summary: A problem an app reports about itself, aggregated by key and count, critical or not, dismissable by the app or by staff.

nodes.name: AppInstallation
nodes.summary: An installation job: app name, manifest URL, requested permissions, brand logo, status and message.

nodes.name: App installation logic
nodes.summary: Fetches and validates a manifest, creates the app with its extensions and webhooks, sends it a token and fetches its brand logo.
nodes.detail: All outbound calls use the hardened Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) client with redirects disabled. The manifest request sends Saleor-Schema-Version and retries connection errors and timeouts twice during installation, adding a second to the connect timeout each time. Brand logos are downloaded in a separate task with a 10 MB limit, an image type check and its own retries.

nodes.name: install_app()
nodes.summary: Creates an App, not yet marked installed, from a validated manifest with its extensions, webhooks and events, sends the token, then fires APP_INSTALLED.
nodes.detail: Overrides the manifest's permissions with the ones granted on the AppInstallation, runs clean_manifest_data with the Saleor version check enforced, creates App with is_installed False, then AppExtension rows and Webhook plus WebhookEvent rows in bulk. When the manifest has tokenTargetUrl it creates a 'Default token' and posts it; if that request fails the app is deleted and the error re-raised. Finally it calls app_installed on a fresh PluginsManager and queues the brand logo download.

token = None
    if tokent_target_url := manifest_data.get("tokenTargetUrl"):
        _, token = app.tokens.create(name="Default token")  # type: ignore[call-arg] # calling create on a related manager # noqa: E501

        try:
            send_app_token(target_url=tokent_target_url, token=token)
        except requests.RequestException as e:
            fetch_brand_data_async(manifest_data, app_installation=app_installation)
            app.delete()
            raise e
    PluginsManager(plugins=settings.PLUGINS).app_installed(app)
    fetch_brand_data_async(manifest_data, app=app)
    return app, token

nodes.name: fetch_manifest()
nodes.summary: Downloads the manifest JSON with Saleor-Schema-Version, no redirects, and optional retries on connection errors and timeouts.

nodes.name: send_app_token()
nodes.summary: Posts {'auth_token': token} to the app's tokenTargetUrl with domain, application programming interface (API) URL and schema version headers, and surfaces the app's error message.

nodes.name: fetch_brand_data_task
nodes.summary: Celery task that downloads the app's brand logo and stores it on the App or AppInstallation, retrying network errors with back-off.

nodes.name: App Celery tasks
nodes.summary: The installation task and the periodic task that hard-deletes soft-deleted apps with their deliveries in batches.
nodes.detail: install_app_task wraps install_app and turns each exception type into a staff-readable message on the AppInstallation (validation errors, the app's own error message, Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) status, connection failure, unknown error). remove_apps_task iterates removed apps one at a time and deletes their event deliveries in id-ordered batches of 1000 with raw deletes to avoid database timeouts, then webhooks, tokens, extensions and the app.

nodes.name: install_app_task
nodes.summary: Runs install_app for an AppInstallation job, deletes the job and marks the app installed on success, or stores a failure message.
nodes.code:
try:
        app, _ = install_app(app_installation, activate=activate)
        app_installation.delete()
        app.is_installed = True
        app.save(update_fields=["is_installed"])
        return
    except ValidationError as e:
        msg = ", ".join([f"{name}: {err}" for name, err in e.message_dict.items()])
        app_installation.message = msg
    except AppInstallationError as e:
        logger.warning("Failed to install app. Error: %s", e)
        app_installation.set_message(str(e))

nodes.name: remove_apps_task
nodes.summary: Periodic task that deletes apps removed longer than DELETE_APP_TTL ago, removing their deliveries, attempts and payloads 1000 at a time with raw deletes.

nodes.name: Manifest validation
nodes.summary: Checks a manifest beyond its schema: Saleor version range, permissions, identifier uniqueness, extensions and webhooks.
nodes.detail: clean_manifest_data first runs the Pydantic ManifestSchema, then collects errors per field: an npm-style requiredSaleorVersion range checked against the running version, permission names mapped to Permission rows, a unique identifier, extension URLs, mounts, targets and permissions, and webhook events, queries, identifiers and headers. It mutates the manifest dict in place into the shape install_app expects and raises one ValidationError with all problems.

nodes.name: ManifestSchema
nodes.summary: Pydantic model of the app manifest: id, name, version, permissions, URLs, token target URL, brand, extensions and webhooks in camelCase.

nodes.name: delete_app()
nodes.summary: Soft-deletes an app (removed_at, is_active False) and fires APP_DELETED, queued or, with force_sync, executed in process.

nodes.name: Saleor request headers
nodes.summary: Header names Saleor sends to apps: Saleor-Domain, Saleor-Event, Saleor-Signature, Saleor-Api-Url, Saleor-Schema-Version, and deprecated X- variants.

nodes.name: App helpers
nodes.summary: Finds active tax apps from their tax webhooks and normalizes an app's deprecation reason.
nodes.detail: get_active_tax_apps unions the apps that have active CHECKOUT_CALCULATE_TAXES or ORDER_CALCULATE_TAXES webhooks, optionally limited to given identifiers. normalize_deprecation_reason strips the text, stores blank as NULL and truncates to 2048 characters so a long reason can never fail an install.

nodes.name: App URL validator
nodes.summary: A URL validator that leaves scheme checks to the caller and accepts localhost, used for webhook targets and manifest URLs.
nodes.detail: AppURLValidator subclasses Django's URLValidator with a regex that accepts any scheme, optional user and password, IPv4, IPv6, hostnames or localhost, and an optional port. Callers pass the allowed schemes, for example http, https, awssqs and gcpubsub for webhook targets.

nodes.name: App Django config and signals
nodes.summary: Connects post-delete signals that remove brand logo files of deleted apps and installations; also holds the row-lock querysets.
nodes.detail: AppConfig.ready connects post_delete signals for App and AppInstallation to delete_brand_images, which queues deletion of the stored logo file. lock_objects provides select_for_update querysets ordered by primary key so concurrent mutations lock app and problem rows in a consistent order.

nodes.name: Sample app manifest
nodes.summary: An example manifest with permissions, two dashboard extensions and a token target URL, for local testing.

nodes.name: App management commands
nodes.summary: Command-line tools to create, install, list, activate, delete apps and toggle webhooks.
nodes.detail: install_app fetches and validates a manifest and runs the same install_app function synchronously, optionally activating the app. create_app makes a local app with permissions and prints or posts its token. app_delete_all soft-deletes every app, optionally dispatching APP_DELETED in process. app_set_active and webhook_set_active flip is_active flags; app_list prints apps.

nodes.name: install_app command
nodes.summary: manage.py install_app <manifest url>: fetches the manifest, creates an AppInstallation and installs synchronously.
nodes.detail: Validates the manifest URL, fetches the manifest with two retries, maps its permissions and, with --quiet, exits if an app with the same identifier exists. It creates an AppInstallation, runs install_app in process, marks the app installed and prints the token as JSON unless quiet; on error it marks the job failed and re-raises.

nodes.name: App schema
nodes.summary: AppQueries (apps, app, appsInstallations, appExtensions, appExtension) and AppMutations, registered in the core GraphQL schema.
nodes.detail: AppQueries resolves apps (filterable and sortable connection), a single app (an app may read itself without MANAGE_APPS), installations and extensions of active apps. AppMutations registers the sixteen app mutations. The schema module also defines the filter input types used by the connections.

nodes.name: App type
nodes.summary: GraphQL App: identity, permissions, tokens, webhooks, extensions, brand, problems, accessToken and circuit breaker state.

nodes.name: AppExtension type
nodes.summary: GraphQL AppExtension with an accessToken for the extension, granted only when the user holds all of the extension's permissions.

nodes.name: resolve_access_token_for_app()
nodes.summary: Issues a JSON Web Token (JWT) for a third-party app's frontend on behalf of the requesting staff user; refused if the app holds MANAGE_APPS.

nodes.name: App resolvers
nodes.summary: Querysets for installed apps, installations and extensions of active apps, and URL stitching for relative popup extension URLs.
nodes.detail: Resolvers use the request's database connection name so reads can go to the replica. resolve_app_extension_url joins a relative extension URL onto the app URL when the target is popup. The access token resolvers delegate to the core JSON Web Token (JWT) helpers after their permission checks.

nodes.name: AppByTokenLoader
nodes.summary: Authenticates app requests: finds tokens by last 4 characters, checks the password hash, and caches token-to-app for 30 days.
nodes.detail: The cache key is an MD5 of the raw token. A cached entry is trusted only when its token id still matches a stored token; tokens not found are evicted from the cache. promise_app only tries this loader for bearer tokens exactly 30 characters long.

nodes.name: App dataloaders
nodes.summary: Batch loaders for apps by id and identifier, apps by event type, tokens, extensions, problems and thumbnails, and get_app_promise.
nodes.detail: Loaders batch by key per request. get_app_promise returns the app already on the context or authenticates the bearer token through AppByTokenLoader. Other loaders fetch active apps by identifier, apps subscribed to an event type, tokens and extensions by app, problems by app and brand logo thumbnails.

nodes.name: App enums
nodes.summary: GraphQL enums for app type, extension mounts and targets, circuit breaker state and who dismissed a problem.

nodes.name: App permission helpers
nodes.summary: Checks that a requestor can grant the permissions it assigns, that MANAGE_APPS is not granted to apps, and that an app is not removed.
nodes.detail: ensure_can_manage_permissions raises when a staff user or app tries to grant permissions it does not hold itself. ensure_app_permissions_allowed blocks MANAGE_APPS for apps. validate_app_is_not_removed turns a removed app into a not-found error. Filters search apps by name, type and extension mount and target.

nodes.name: App mutations
nodes.summary: Sixteen mutations that install, create, update, activate, delete apps, manage tokens and problems, and reset the circuit breaker.
nodes.detail: Most need MANAGE_APPS; appInstall also requires a staff user. Mutations that change an app fire the matching lifecycle event through the plugin manager with call_event, so webhooks go out after the transaction commits.

nodes.name: appInstall mutation
nodes.summary: Validates the manifest URL and permissions, creates an AppInstallation job and queues install_app_task.

nodes.name: appFetchManifest mutation
nodes.summary: Fetches and validates a manifest without installing, returning it with brand data for review.

nodes.name: appTokenCreate mutation
nodes.summary: Creates a new token for an app the requestor may manage and returns the raw token once.

nodes.name: appTokenVerify mutation
nodes.summary: Reports whether a raw token belongs to an active, non-removed app, checking hashes of tokens with the same last 4 characters.

nodes.name: appTokenDelete mutation

nodes.name: appCreate mutation
nodes.summary: Creates a local app with permissions and a default token, then fires APP_INSTALLED.

nodes.summary: Lets the calling app update its own fields, such as its deprecation reason.

nodes.name: Webhook schema
nodes.summary: WebhookQueries (webhook, webhookEvents, webhookSamplePayload) and WebhookMutations, registered in the core GraphQL schema.
nodes.detail: WebhookQueries resolves a webhook for its owning app or a MANAGE_APPS user, the deprecated webhookEvents list and webhookSamplePayload, which checks the event's permission against the app or user before building a sample. WebhookMutations registers the six webhook mutations.

nodes.name: Webhook GraphQL types
nodes.summary: GraphQL Webhook, WebhookEvent, EventDelivery and EventDeliveryAttempt types, with filterable, sortable delivery connections.
nodes.detail: Webhook exposes events split into asyncEvents and syncEvents, the subscription query, custom headers, active flag and a paginated eventDeliveries connection. EventDelivery exposes status, event type, payload (loaded by id through a dataloader) and attempts; EventDeliveryAttempt exposes duration, response, headers and status code. Filters and sorters let the dashboard list failed deliveries.

nodes.name: Webhook resolvers
nodes.summary: Resolves a webhook for its owner app or a MANAGE_APPS user, lists deprecated event types, and returns sample payloads after a permission check.
nodes.detail: resolve_webhook returns the webhook only if it belongs to the calling app, or if the user holds MANAGE_APPS and the webhook's app is not removed; otherwise it raises PermissionDenied. resolve_sample_payload checks the event's permission against the app or user before generating a sample.

nodes.name: Webhook event enums
nodes.summary: Generates WebhookEventTypeAsyncEnum, WebhookEventTypeSyncEnum and related enums from the event catalogue, with per-event descriptions.
nodes.detail: Builds graphene enums at import from the event CHOICES lists, attaching a description per event from WEBHOOK_EVENT_DESCRIPTION and deprecation reasons for legacy payment and export events. Also defines EventDeliveryStatusEnum and WebhookPayloadGenerationEnum.

nodes.name: Webhook dataloaders
nodes.summary: Batch loaders for payloads by id, webhook events by webhook, webhooks by app or event type, and active webhooks.
nodes.detail: PayloadByIdLoader fetches payload text for EventDelivery.payload. WebhookEventsByWebhookIdLoader, WebhooksByAppIdLoader, WebhooksByEventTypeLoader and ActiveWebhooksByIdLoader batch the lookups the types and other dataloaders need.

nodes.name: Webhook mutations
nodes.summary: Create, update, delete, dry-run and trigger webhooks, and retry an event delivery.
nodes.detail: Create and update need MANAGE_APPS or an authenticated app, which may only touch its own webhooks. Dry run needs a staff user with the event's permission. utils.get_webhook_object_id resolves ids for the delete and update mutations.

nodes.name: webhookCreate mutation
nodes.summary: Validates app, subscription query, channel filter (up to 500 slugs) and custom headers, then saves the Webhook and its WebhookEvent rows.

nodes.name: webhookUpdate mutation
nodes.summary: Updates a webhook with the same validation as create and replaces its event rows when events change.

nodes.name: webhookDelete mutation
nodes.summary: Deletes a webhook owned by the calling app or, for MANAGE_APPS users, any webhook of a non-removed app.

nodes.name: webhookDryRun mutation
nodes.summary: Resolves a subscription query against a real object and returns the payload without creating a delivery or sending anything.

nodes.name: webhookTrigger mutation
nodes.summary: Sends one real delivery of an asynchronous event for a given object to one webhook, running the sender task in the request.
nodes.detail: For deferred events with deferred payload generation it saves a payload-less delivery and queues generate_deferred_payloads. Otherwise it builds the delivery and calls send_webhook_request_async directly (not through Celery); a Celery Retry raised by a failed attempt marks the delivery failed.

nodes.name: eventDeliveryRetry mutation

nodes.name: Plugin schema
nodes.summary: The plugin and plugins queries and the pluginUpdate mutation, all requiring MANAGE_PLUGINS.
nodes.detail: Both queries are wrapped in plugin_manager_promise_callback so they receive the request's plugin manager. resolve_plugins aggregates configurations across channels, applies the filter (active, type, name) and sort, and returns a connection slice.

nodes.name: pluginUpdate mutation
nodes.summary: Saves active flag and configuration for a plugin, globally or for one channel, refusing a channel for global plugins and vice versa.

nodes.name: Plugin resolvers
nodes.summary: Aggregates each plugin's global and per-channel configurations, hides secret field values, and filters and sorts the list.
nodes.detail: aggregate_plugins_configuration loads all plugins and groups global and per-channel instances by plugin id. Before returning, hide_private_configuration_fields blanks password fields and shows only the last 4 characters of secret fields. Filters match on active state per channel, global or per-channel type, and name.

nodes.summary: Gives a request its PluginsManager, one per requestor (app, user or anonymous), built through dataloaders and honoring allow_replica.

nodes.name: Plugin GraphQL types
nodes.summary: Plugin, PluginConfiguration and ConfigurationItem types, with enums, filters and sorters for the plugins list.
nodes.detail: Plugin exposes id, name, description, global configuration and per-channel configurations; each configuration lists ConfigurationItem name, value, type, help text and label. The plugin manager dataloaders in the same package build one manager per requestor and an anonymous one when nobody is signed in.

nodes.name: PluginsManager module
nodes.summary: The PluginsManager class with one method per hook (about 200) and get_plugins_manager, the factory the rest of Saleor uses.
nodes.detail: The file defines PluginsManager with hook methods grouped by domain (taxes, customers, products, orders, checkouts, payments, transactions, notifications, external authentication) and get_plugins_manager. Imports of models are kept under TYPE_CHECKING to avoid import cycles. Plugins are loaded on first use, not at construction.

nodes.name: PluginsManager
nodes.summary: Loads plugins lazily per channel and exposes every hook: taxes, payments, notifications and all webhook events.
nodes.detail: Each hook method names the plugin method, a default value and the channel slug, then calls __run_method_on_plugins. Tax methods stop at the first plugin that returns a value. Payment methods route to the plugin whose id matches the gateway, including app gateway ids via WebhookPlugin.check_plugin_id. Many hook methods carry a note that webhook functionality will move from plugins into core modules.

nodes.name: PluginsManager._ensure_channel_plugins_loaded()
nodes.summary: Imports plugin classes from settings.PLUGINS and instantiates global ones once and channel ones per channel slug with their database configuration.

nodes.name: PluginsManager.__run_method_on_plugins()
nodes.summary: Runs a named hook on each active plugin for the channel, passing the previous plugin's result as previous_value.

nodes.name: PluginsManager.webhook()
nodes.summary: Routes a /plugins/ request to the matching active plugin's webhook method with the rest of the path, or answers 404.

nodes.name: PluginsManager.notify()
nodes.summary: Sends a notify event with a lazy payload function to one plugin or to all plugins for a channel.

nodes.name: get_plugins_manager()
nodes.summary: Creates a PluginsManager for settings.PLUGINS with a requestor getter, forcing the writer database when replicas are not allowed.

nodes.name: BasePlugin
nodes.summary: Base class for plugins: id, name, configuration structure and defaults, per-channel flag, and typed declarations of every hook a plugin may implement.
nodes.detail: Hooks are declared as annotations, not methods, so a plugin implements only what it needs and the manager skips the rest. Configuration is a list of name and value pairs merged with CONFIG_STRUCTURE for labels and types; secret fields are hidden in the application programming interface (API). save_plugin_configuration validates and persists a PluginConfiguration row.

nodes.name: Plugin configuration models
nodes.summary: PluginConfiguration (identifier, channel, active, JSON configuration; unique per identifier and channel) and EmailTemplate rows.
nodes.detail: PluginConfiguration stores one row per plugin identifier and channel (null for global), with active flag and a JSON list of name and value pairs; it also declares the MANAGE_PLUGINS permission. EmailTemplate stores a named template body for a plugin configuration, used by the email plugins.

nodes.name: Plugin HTTP views
nodes.summary: Three Django views behind /plugins/ URLs that build a writer-database plugin manager and pass the request to a plugin's webhook method.
nodes.detail: Each view is wrapped in allow_writer and builds a plugin manager that reads the primary database, then calls PluginsManager.webhook or webhook_endpoint_without_channel. The manager splits the request path after the plugin id and passes the remainder to the plugin's webhook method, answering 404 when no active plugin matches.

nodes.name: Plugin Django config
nodes.summary: At start-up imports every plugin path in settings.PLUGINS and fails if a plugin lacks PLUGIN_ID; also plugin module discovery.
nodes.detail: PluginConfig.ready imports every class path in settings.PLUGINS and raises ImproperlyConfigured if a plugin lacks PLUGIN_ID, so a bad plugin setting stops start-up. discover_plugins_modules returns the packages of the configured plugins. const and error_codes hold the app id prefix and plugin error codes.

nodes.name: WebhookPlugin
nodes.summary: The plugin with id 'mirumee.webhooks', forced active, implementing about 200 hooks as webhook triggers.

flows.name: An app is installed from its manifest and subscribes to events
flows.summary: Staff install an app by manifest URL; a background task fetches and validates the manifest, creates the app and its webhooks, hands over a token and announces APP_INSTALLED.

steps.text: The dashboard sends the appInstall mutation with an app name, manifest URL and the permissions staff agreed to grant.
AppInstall checks the manifest URL and that the requestor may grant those permissions, saves an AppInstallation job and queues install_app_task.
A Celery worker picks up the job and calls install_app; on any failure it stores a readable message on the job instead.
Saleor downloads the manifest JSON, without following redirects and with up to two retries on connection errors.
The manifest is validated: schema, Saleor version range, permissions, unique identifier, extensions, and each webhook's events and subscription query.
The App is created with the granted permissions, then its dashboard extensions, Webhook rows and WebhookEvent subscriptions.
Each webhook stores its target URL, subscription query, custom headers and channel filter; from now on selection queries find it.
A default token is created and posted to the app's tokenTargetUrl; if that fails the new app is deleted again.
The plugin manager's app_installed hook reaches WebhookPlugin, which sends APP_INSTALLED to the new app's own webhooks.
The event is stored and queued like any other asynchronous webhook; the task then marks the app installed and deletes the job.

flows.name: An order event becomes an asynchronous webhook delivered with retries
flows.summary: Creating an order fans out through the plugin manager to WebhookPlugin, which stores deliveries and lets Celery send them, retrying failures with back-off.

steps.text: Order code selects webhooks for ORDER_CREATED and calls the plugin manager's order_created method after the database transaction commits.
The manager runs order_created on every active plugin for the order's channel, passing previous_value along.
WebhookPlugin keeps webhooks whose channel filter matches the order and prepares a lazy legacy payload generator.
Subscription webhooks set to deferred generation get payload-less EventDelivery rows; legacy and immediate ones get EventPayload rows too.
A Celery task waits until the deliveries are visible on the read replica, reloads the order and resolves each app's subscription query.
Each query runs against the GraphQL schema as the receiving app, so the payload holds only fields that app asked for and may read.
send_webhook_request_async loads the delivery, skips inactive apps, records an attempt and sends the payload.
The payload is signed and sent by Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) POST, Amazon Simple Queue Service (SQS) message or Google Pub/Sub publish, depending on the target URL.
On a failure other than a 3xx or 4xx answer, Celery retries with a countdown of 10 seconds doubled per try, up to 5 retries, then the delivery is marked failed.
Each attempt is reported to observability webhooks when observability is enabled.
After a 2xx answer the delivery and its payload are deleted, so only failed or pending deliveries stay in the database.

flows.name: A synchronous tax webhook, guarded by the circuit breaker
flows.summary: Checkout tax calculation asks a tax app for prices and waits for its answer, with the circuit breaker skipping apps that keep failing.

steps.text: Tax code finds the tax app's CHECKOUT_CALCULATE_TAXES webhook and calls trigger_webhook_sync_promise with a static payload as fallback.
When the breaker board is enabled and the event is monitored, an open breaker resolves to None at once; otherwise the call goes ahead and its outcome is counted.
The app's subscription query is resolved into an unsaved EventPayload and EventDelivery.
send_webhook_request_sync posts the signed payload and waits up to 18 seconds for the answer.
For the AvaTax app, the request lands on its checkout tax route, which answers with line and shipping taxes.
The body is parsed as JSON; failures are saved with their attempt for inspection, successes leave no rows.
Tax code validates the answer with CalculateTaxesSchema before applying the taxes to the checkout.
